concerns.text: The readability metrics (BLEU, ROUGE‑L, Sentence‑BERT similarity) are computed by comparing each comment variant to the *human‑written docstring* (the reference). For the human‑comment condition this yields perfect scores (BLEU = 1, ROUGE‑L = 1, similarity = 1) and for the no‑comment condition yields near‑zero scores. Consequently the metric values are deterministic functions of the experimental condition, not independent predictors of human performance. Correlating these metrics with the human outcomes (completion time, accuracy, helpfulness) therefore measures a tautological relationship: the metric encodes the condition, and the condition drives the outcomes. This circular validation prevents any meaningful assessment of whether the metrics truly reflect readability or predict developer performance.
